title: Bazira (Barikot Ghundai)
subtitle: Indo-Greek city and Italian excavations at Barikot, Lower Swat
edits: A bench up to 24 m wide is cut along the jeep track to the smoothed track profile (the 30 m DSM includes tree canopy).
Road bumps and ruts in the drive are illustrative; the grade and the line of the track are real.
Trees, shrubs, grass tufts and boulders are placed where WorldCover maps that cover; their size and number are illustrative.
The walking loop is a 150 m circle around the arrival point; it is not a mapped trail.

The excavated area is drawn from the Commons photos (Fawad002, Fazal.Khaliq, Jona Lendering): a grid of low wall foundations on blocks about 14 by 11 m with 5 m streets between, 0.6 to 1.6 m high, with some blocks dug (darker floors) and some left as ground. The grid, the block sizes, the wall heights and which blocks are dug are estimated.
The dug floors are darker flat patches on the surface: the page cannot cut the DEM, so the trench depth is not drawn.

The city wall is estimated: a square about 250 m a side (about 6 ha, close to the 7 ha of the lower city without the acropolis that Wikipedia gives), 1.5 m high foundations, 3 m thick, with rectangular bastions about 8 m along and 4 m proud of the wall, five per side. Wikipedia says the wall had massive rectangular bastions; its line, its size and the bastion spacing are not in the sources.
The site point is the OSM node Ancient Bazira (historic=archaeological_site, Wikidata Q3634988), 0 m away. The hill behind the dig is the DEM terrain, not a model.

The trailhead is the end of the OSM Mingora Road way nearest the site, about 270 m away. The walk is traced over the DEM only; it crosses the Swat river channel on the way (OSM river ways), not at the mapped ford.
The OSM archaeological_site outline about 260 m south-west of the point (a 70 m polygon) is not drawn: its meaning is not known.
The walk from the end of the jeep track follows the mapped OSM footpath for 0.0 km; the last 0.28 km is not mapped and is traced over the ground (easiest slope on the DEM).
Season colours, snow, ice and dawn mist are illustrative.

Traffic on the drive is illustrative: the vehicle kinds are those seen on Swat roads (Willys jeeps, Hilux, Suzuki vans, Mehran cars, CD70 motorbikes, Qingqi rickshaws, painted trucks); their number and movement are not counted.
